Public domain: every person whose words are in this text died in 1925 or earlier, so the term has ended under the law of every country, whichever one first published it.

People: James Fergusson (author, Wikidata Q1225014), died 1886; Richard Phené Spiers (editor, Wikidata Q1571225), died 1916. They are every person Project Gutenberg's catalog lists for the book ("Fergusson, James, 1808-1886; Spiers, Richard Phené, 1838-1916 [Editor]") and every person the printed edition's opening pages credit; each death year is Wikidata's.

Printed edition: A history of ancient and medieval architecture, London : Murray, 1893, the Internet Archive scan https://archive.org/details/historyofancient01ferg. Three passages of the Gutenberg text have 96%, 75%, 76% of their four-word runs in the scan's text. The scan does not show the credit of Richard Phené Spiers, whom the catalog lists; the passages show the scan holds this text.
